title: Mainly dry and warm weather expected in most parts of the island
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at a few places in Sabaragamuwa province and in Colombo, Kaluthara, Galle, and Matara districts after 2.00 pm, today (29), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Yemen’s Houthis enter Iran war with attacks on Israel, while US Marines arrive in region
byline: The risk of an expanded Iran war grew as Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis on Saturday launched their first attacks on Israel since the start of the conflict, even as additional U.S. forces reached the Middle East.

title: Iran threatens to target Israeli and American universities in Middle East
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRCG) has threatened to target Israeli and American universities in the Middle East, following the attack on the University of Science and Technology in Tehran.

title: Two suspects arrested for aiding and abetting drug trafficking after deportation from India
byline: Two suspects who aided and abetted drug trafficking have been arrested by the Western Province North Crimes Division.

title: Iran will allow more Pakistani ships through Strait of Hormuz
byline: Pakistan’s foreign minister said late Saturday that Iran has agreed to allow 20 additional Pakistani-flagged ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Centralized electronic system for asset and liability declarations to launch on March 31
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has taken steps to open a centralized electronic system for asset and liability declarations to declarants.

title: Two Australian states offer free public transport to ease fuel pain
byline: Australians in two states will be able to travel on public transport for free to take pressure off household budgets as fuel costs surge.

title: No Kings protests across the US rally against Donald Trump
byline: Large protests against the Trump administration are taking place in cities across the US, marking the third iteration of No Kings rallies that have previously drawn crowds into the millions.

title: Revised bus fares must be displayed inside buses – Officials
byline: The Western Province Road Passenger Transport Authority states that it is mandatory to display the revised bus fares inside all buses for passengers.

title: Pentagon preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran, Washington Post reports
byline: The Pentagon is preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran, the Washington Post reported Saturday, citing U.S. officials.

title: Bahrain aluminium smelter confirms Iranian attack
byline: Aluminium Bahrain (Alba) says two of its workers sustained minor injuries in an Iranian attack on its smelter, one of the world’s biggest, on Saturday.

title: 7-year-old boy killed in road accident in Thanamalwila
byline: A fatal road accident has been reported near Kuda Oya town along the Thanamalwila–Wellawaya road.

title: Sri Lanka’s judiciary enters digital age with landmark paperless trial
byline: Sri Lanka’s judiciary has taken a transformative step in its history by conducting a paperless court hearing based entirely on a digital system on March 26 at the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka.

title: Minister Handunnetti pledges legal measures over low-priced imported goods
byline: Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, Sunil Handunnetti, stated that legislation will soon be formulated to take action against those selling imported goods at prices lower than local products.

title: PM Modi thanks Gulf nations for assistance amid West Asia conflict; says ‘‘no place for self-serving politics"
byline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday expressed gratitude towards Gulf nations for assistance to Indians residing there amid the West Asia conflict and noted that India is facing the global fuel crisis resolutely.

title: 33-year-old woman arrested for hoarding petrol and diesel in Kuda Oya
byline: A 33-year-old woman has been arrested by the Kuda Oya Police for allegedly hoarding a stock of fuel at her residence.

title: State of Public Emergency in Sri Lanka extended by one month
byline: The State of Public Emergency in Sri Lanka, declared by the President, has been extended by one month.

title: Monaragala PS Income Inspector arrested over Rs. 50,000 fraud
byline: An income inspector of the Monaragala Pradeshiya Sabha has been arrested in connection with a financial fraud, police stated.

title: Iran’s foreign minister says journalists’ deaths ‘a serious wake-up call’
byline: Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi says the deaths of three journalists in Lebanon are “not only a deep loss for the media community in the region and the world, but also a serious wake-up call for the global conscience”.

title: Legal action against traders for hoarding rice, refusing retail sales
byline: Steps have been taken to file cases before the Maligakanda Magistrate’s Court against several traders accused of hoarding rice and refusing to sell it at retail prices.

title: President AKD appreciates India’s support in addressing ongoing energy crisis
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has expressed his gratitude to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the government of India for the support extended to Sri Lanka amidst the ongoing energy crisis.

title: Over 630 arrested in island-wide anti-drug raids
byline: Police have arrested 635 suspects island-wide yesterday (28) through daily search operations launched to curb crime and drug-related activities, police said.

title: Israeli military days away from hitting all its “top priority” targets in Iran
byline: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) is days away from hitting all the targets in Iran it classes as “top priority,” a spokesperson said today.

title: Pakistan capital beefs up security ahead of high-level talks
byline: The foreign ministers of Egypt and Turkey are in Pakistan, with Saudi Arabia’s foreign minister expected to arrive in the coming hours for four-way talks on regional issues, including de-escalating the US and Israeli war with Iran.

title: 11 arrested over illegal street racing, betting in Piliyandala
byline: Eleven individuals have been arrested for engaging in illegal motorcycle and three-wheeler racing linked to betting activities along the Kesbewa alternative road in Piliyandala, police said.

title: Earthquake of magnitude 4.3 strikes Tibet
byline: An earthquake of magnitude 4.3 struck Tibet on Sunday, a statement by the National Center for Seismology (NCS) said.

title: Saudi Arabia extends visa deadlines as gulf travel turmoil deepens
byline: Travelers stranded across the Gulf by airspace closures and airport disruptions are receiving crucial visa relief, as Saudi Arabia joins Qatar and Kuwait in extending deadlines and relaxing penalties for visitors whose permitted stays are expiring mid-crisis.

title: Pope Leo says God rejects prayers of leaders who wage wars
byline: Pope Leo said on Sunday that God rejects the prayers of leaders who start wars and have “hands full of blood”, in unusually forceful remarks as the Iran war entered its second month.

title: Gem businessman missing in Kahawatta; Police launch probe
byline: Kahawatta Police have launched an investigation into the disappearance of a gem businessman.

title: Iran parliament speaker says US planning ground attack
byline: Iran’s parliament speaker on Sunday (Mar 29) accused the United States of plotting a ground attack despite talking about diplomacy, after a US warship with around 3,500 military personnel arrived in the Middle East.

title: Ukrainian President says Russia conducted surveillance on US military bases for Iran
byline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said that he has received intelligence on Russia conducting surveillance of US bases in the Middle East and Gulf regions.

title: “Surakimu Lanka” national programme for energy security launched
byline: The national programme titled “Surakimu Lanka”, designed to encourage the public to use energy sparingly, was officially launched today (29).

title: Belavia announces flights to Mattala in April
byline: The Belavia Airline has announced flights to Mattala International Airport from the Minsk National Airport in April.

title: Registration of Persons Dept. issues notice on resumption of services
byline: The Department for Registration of Persons has announced that efforts to restore its computer systems are ongoing.

title: Bahrain announces maritime ban to protect country’s coasts
byline: Bahrain has announced a maritime ban which it says will be in place “until further notice” to protect the Gulf nation’s coasts, amid ongoing attacks from Iran.

title: Talks on Iran war between Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan conclude
byline: Pakistan hosted talks with Turkey, Egypt and Saudi Arabia on Sunday as part of its efforts to broker an end to the Iran war, with initial discussions focused on proposals to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping, sources familiar with the matter said.

title: NASA Artemis II astronauts arrive in Florida for first crewed Moon mission in decades
byline: The four astronauts selected for NASA’s Artemis II mission have arrived in Florida, entering the final phase of preparations for the first crewed journey towards the Moon in more than five decades.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for several provinces
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Eastern, North-western, Northern and North-central provinces and in Monaragala district.

title: Escalating Red Sea tensions pose new risks to Sri Lanka’s economy – Sajith
byline: Given the escalating situation in the Middle East, there could be disruptions in the transportation of essential goods to the Asian region in the future, which may lead to an unexpected rise in inflation in Sri Lanka, according to the Leader of the Opposition, Sajith Premadasa.

title: Talks begin between Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to discuss de-escalating war
byline: High-level talks between the foreign ministers representing Egypt, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have begun.

title: Govt. underscores broader significance of India’s role in the region
byline: India’s support in maintaining fuel supplies to Sri Lanka during a period of global uncertainty has been acknowledged by the Sri Lankan government as a timely intervention that helped ease pressure on essential energy needs.

title: Mojtaba Khamenei thanks Iraq for support during war
byline: Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, thanked the Iraqi paramilitary groups that have been targeting American bases in the Middle East since the war began a month ago, semi-official IRGC-linked Tasnim News Agency reported.

title: Notorious gang member Midigama Chuti to be brought back to Sri Lanka tomorrow
byline: Prabhath Madusanka, also known as ‘Midigama Chuti,’ a member of an organized criminal gang who was taken into custody in Oman, is scheduled to be brought back to the country tomorrow morning (30).

title: Israeli PM Netanyahu orders expansion of Israeli buffer zone in southern Lebanon
byline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he has ordered the expansion of Israel’s security buffer zone in southern Lebanon with the aim of repelling Lebanese cross-border attacks.

title: UAE official demands compensation from Iran
byline: A senior United Arab Emirates (UAE) official has called for Iranian compensation for the damage caused to the country due to Tehran’s strikes.

title: Sacred sapling of Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi in Bendigo added to Australia’s National Trust Register of Significant Trees
byline: The sacred sapling of the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi, which was brought from Sri Lanka and planted at the Sri Bodhi Dhamma Vihara in Bendigo, Australia has been officially added to the National Trust Register of Significant Trees.

title: Sri Lanka’s tourist arrivals in 2026 surpass 700,000
byline: The number of tourist arrivals in Sri Lanka in 2026 has crossed the 700,000-mark, the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) stated.
